summary: House passage of H.R.33 with broad bipartisan support (423-1) and a Senate companion introduced (SB199) signals cross-chamber momentum.
Objections highlight a Senate gating risk and the tight timeline before May 1, 2026, which could stall enactment despite House action.
Policy diplomacy addressing double taxation and ongoing administration negotiations provide a favorable context that could accelerate movement.
Historical federal-bill enactment rates are low (~6%), which argues for modest expectations even with House momentum.
